card.label: 深色导视标记
card.thesis: 用稳定的方向标记和明确的状态色，在内容与上下文之间保持定位感。
materials: 精确的细线与状态标记
card.viewport: 深蓝框架内保留正常网格与 Inspector；当前对象使用同一种钴蓝标记，错误与警告另有语义颜色。
card.case: 操作定位很清楚，但配色需要约束，避免每类信息都争夺注意力。
card.risk: 多种状态色若同时大量出现，会比前两种更忙。
card.imageBrief: Midnight wayfinding-inspired professional desktop media tool, adapted strictly as Operate UI. Midnight blue #07192E canvas, deeper blue panel #112E4B, near-white #EAF0F5 labels, cobalt #3B80D7 selection/focus, scarlet #D85753 only actual errors, amber #D6AE58 only warning. Familiar sans/CJK controls; use small consistent colored current-subject markers across selected card and Inspector title. Media remains full color. Fine rules, rectangular low-radius controls, concise small captions. Preserve normal library grid, tool header and aligned property inspector. No railway map, stations, route connections, train icons, transport names, map canvas, equipment frames, travel hero or decorative colored network. The inspiration provides palette, readability and one subject marker only.

prompt:
Create a high-fidelity professional desktop application UI design comp. This is one decision comp in an attended Impeccable direction round, not an approved production comp and not a build-phase asset. The decision server is started before your image generation. Render ONE complete Locus app viewport at desktop landscape 1440x900 (or closest supported aspect), same structural regions and sample content as siblings, focusing detail on Entity cards and Inspector. The user wants incremental mixed image/code exploration; no global buildPath is selected. Do not redesign navigation or add functions. The direction is not approved yet.
STRUCTURE: slim 40px Locus top titlebar with history arrows and small 导入 action; 48px left navigation rail for 内容, 标签, 设置; compact content toolbar with 内容, 筛选, refresh icon. Main area is a 3-column by 2-row content grid taking about 65% of available width and a 320px Inspector taking the rest, separated by one resize divider. Minimal bottom task/notification status. Inspector uses a quiet section header and normal short property rows, not stacked dashboard cards. No oversized card footer or giant call-to-action.
SAMPLE CONTENT: The viewport must be visibly marked 示例内容 once, because these are synthetic design samples. Six items use simple media previews: mountain landscape, city portrait scene, botanical illustration, video frame with a tiny duration, document.txt, model.safetensors. Selected item is landscape.png. These are illustrative visual content, not claimed user records. Inspector for the selected item shows 标题 landscape.png; 类型 PNG; 尺寸 960 × 540; 个人标签 with two small sample tags 风景 and 参考 plus a small inline +; 备注 with a compact editable text field; 组件 with 文件 and 图像 entries; 标识 with a shortened UUID and a copy icon. One ordinary quiet status 已保存 is sufficient. Original filenames stay Latin, UI labels are Simplified Chinese. No prices, customers, dates, claims, metadata provenance or generation relationships. Preserve real app capabilities only. Body and property text must remain legible at desktop scale; don't fake an empty layout with placeholders.
OPERATE COMPS RULES:
The comp is the product screen, in the direction's committed palette: its shell and navigation with a distinct area for each job and, where there is data, filters over what they scope and charts and tables with clear states. The world enters only through type, palette, density, and the one signature move; it never supplies the page's organisation, so a working screen never reads as a newspaper, a poster, or any other artifact of the world. Every control is a standard one the visitor already knows how to use, a web component on the web and the platform's native control in an app: buttons, tabs, inputs, selects, filters, tables with sortable headers, navigation that reads as navigation. Never a costume of the world's own interface: a terminal's function-key bar or command prompt, an instrument's bezel, ruled ledger paper standing in for a table. A comp an engineer could not build from the platform's standard components is a picture of the tool, not the tool. The finish bar is the best product in the category: an aligned grid, consistent spacing, a real type scale, and clear hierarchy. The signature move adds to a screen that is already that clean; it never stands in for it.
Prompt with the screen's real content: the product name, realistic data with plausible values and units, real labels, and one state worth seeing (an alert, a degraded service, an empty filter result), never placeholder tiles.
Comps two and three vary the product's organisation, never its world coverage: the navigation model (side rail, top bar, command-first), how the work areas divide the screen, which data leads, the density, and where the signature move sits. Each must be recognisably different from the first at thumbnail size; a variant only its prompt can tell apart adds no choice. A variant that adds world material, texture, or ornament goes further in the wrong direction; on a working screen, more world is a costume.
Self-check every render: with the name covered, does it read as a product of its category, could the visitor do the task from it, and is it at least as clean as the category standard and more distinctive than it? If it reads as an artifact of the world first, regenerate with the shell and the work areas named region by region and the world held to its four contributions.
These are sibling DIRECTION comps with a deliberately shared first surface, not the later three-composition build round. Do not generate extra variants. Render UI edge to edge, no device/browser frame, no desktop/desk around it.
